entity.summary: Non-custodial multisignature Bitcoin and Ethereum vault service in which users control the signing quorum while Casa holds one emergency recovery key that cannot move funds by itself.

system_components.custody_note: Held by the user on the mobile device.
One or more user-controlled hardware-wallet keys participate in the multisig quorum.
Casa holds one recovery key, but that key alone cannot move funds or satisfy the multisig quorum.

entity.notes: Casa explicitly calls the vault non-custodial because Casa never holds enough keys to move funds. WLR still records `custody_model=hybrid` to preserve the material provider-held recovery-key component rather than flattening the architecture into a pure user-only key model.

products.summary: Casa Standard 2-of-3 multisig vault using a user mobile key, a user hardware key and a Casa-held recovery key, where any two signatures are required.
products.notes: Selected vault product rather than treating Casa's advisory/service layer as a wallet. Casa holds only one of three keys and cannot move funds unilaterally.

evidence.title: What is a bitcoin wallet?
evidence.notes: Current Casa support describes Casa as non-custodial, explains 2-of-3/3-of-5 vaults, and states Casa holds one Recovery Key that cannot move funds alone.

evidence.title: What is the Casa app?
evidence.notes: First-party Casa support defines the 3-key vault as a 2-of-3 multisig arrangement and says Casa holds only one emergency recovery key, insufficient to send funds by itself.
